speaker: abel_garnish
text: The plot is on the door. Errors, this afternoon. You speak, and then the plot has you off.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I know the shape of it. I speak, and then I sit.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Two hours, by my hose, in a parlour that has never heard of a fire. Marry, I would rather have your silence than your speech, if the speech is the old man's.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You will have both. The speech first.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Let him have the first of it, Will. Thou art not the one who has to stand still afterwards.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I never stand still. That is why the yard likes me.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: The book is not to be mended this morning. Say what you have, and sit where the plot sits you.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not rewrite him before dinner. He has survived worse rooms than this.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Say the opening, then. I will hear whether the room takes it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is a long tale of a ship and a son, and I will not give you all of it before the yard does.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Give us the end of the breath, then. I' faith, a man likes to know when he may come on.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Your cue is the old man's last word, and not before. I have it on the plot.

speaker: will_kemp
text: And if he takes two hours over the last word?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The two hours are not the speech. The speech ends. Then I wait, and the play goes on without me.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: So thou art in it, and then thou art a man in a cold room.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That is the part. I have played it.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Then we will not discover it again. Masters, the entrances as they are written. No new cuts.

speaker: will_kemp
text: No new cuts, and no new fire. I shall hop to keep warm, and the book may disapprove.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Hop on your own side of the plot. His side is a chair.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Take the chair near the yard door, Will. That is the colder one.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I had the colder one last time. I can find it again.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Last time you looked like a man who had lost a boat and two sons. Do it so again, and leave me the laugh.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The laugh is yours. The waiting is mine.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Good. That is all this scene needs. The rest of you, the middle, and do not send for him.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: We will not send. Thou wilt hear us through the wall, and come when the plot says.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will hear you. I will not come early.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Then I am satisfied. By my hose, a quiet old man is the best partner, so long as he is quiet in the right hour.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: The plot stays on the door. Nobody takes it down to improve it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave it. I am going home to a page of my own before I come back to sit.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: A page of thine own. Keep it under thine arm, if thou must. Do not read it at us.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I was not going to.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Read it at the yard and they will think it a proclamation. Marry, save it.

speaker: abel_garnish
text: Off the door, then. We are done with the old man until the play wants him.
